title: Lowest Common Ancestor
description: Given a binary search tree (BST) and two node values `p` and `q`, find the Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA) node value.
input_format: First line contains `n`, `p`, and `q`. Second line contains level order tokens of BST.

sample_tests.explanation: LCA of 2 and 4 is 2 (node can be ancestor of itself).

hints: Take advantage of BST properties: left < root < right.
If both p and q are less than current node, the LCA must be in the left subtree.
If they split on opposite sides, the current node is the LCA.

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n, p, q = int(data[0]), int(data[1]), int(data[2])
    tokens = data[3:3+n]
    class Node:
        def __init__(self, v): self.v = int(v); self.left = None; self.right = None
    from collections import deque
    root = Node(tokens[0])
    qu = deque([root])
    idx = 1
    while qu and idx < len(tokens):
        curr = qu.popleft()
        if idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx] != 'null':
            curr.left = Node(tokens[idx]); qu.append(curr.left)
        idx += 1
        if idx < len(tokens) and tokens[idx] != 'null':
            curr.right = Node(tokens[idx]); qu.append(curr.right)
        idx += 1
    curr = root
    while curr:
        if p < curr.v and q < curr.v: curr = curr.left
        elif p > curr.v and q > curr.v: curr = curr.right
        else: print(curr.v); break
